articles.headline: Timberwolves' Anthony Edwards undergoes successful knee scope
articles.description: Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards underwent a "successful" arthroscopic procedure on his ailing right knee at the Mayo Clinic on Thursday, the team announced.
articles.headlineJa: ティンバーウルブズのアンソニー・エドワーズ、膝の関節鏡手術に成功
articles.descriptionJa: ティンバーウルブズのスター、アンソニー・エドワーズが木曜日にメイヨークリニックで不調だった右膝の関節鏡手術を受け、成功したことをチームが発表した。
articles.body:
Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards underwent a "successful" arthroscopic procedure on his ailing right knee at the Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minn. on Thursday, the team announced.

Edwards had a debridement procedure performed on his knee, which is a minimally invasive measure used to clean, smooth, or remove damaged cartilage, bone spurs, or loose joint fragments from the knee joint to relieve pain and improve mobility, according to the Mayo Clinic.

The team's statement said Edwards is expected to make a full recover but did not denote a timeframe for his potential return. Sources tell ESPN's Shams Charania that Edwards could be sidelined up to two months.

Speaking before Wednesday night's loss to the Warriors, Timberwolves president of basketball operations Tim Connelly said he expects Edwards to be "good as new" when he eventually returns to game action.

Edwards has been bothered by right knee pain since last spring and was limited to a career-low 61 games last season. He was seen grabbing his knee and grimacing at one point during Sunday's home opener against the Toronto Raptors. Even after being listed as questionable to play Monday, Edwards scored 47 points in an overtime loss at Cleveland. His 133 points through four games is a franchise record.

An MRI on Tuesday revealed new damage for Edwards that was not detected in previous scans, which were done before training camp and during the playoffs. His condition this summer was not such that a procedure would have been recommended then, Connelly said Wednesday.

"We're just concerned about his long-term health," Connelly added. "We want to make sure we're putting him in the best position he can be so he can be the best version he's going to be for a long time.

"He's bummed, but Anthony is such a naturally positive and upbeat guy. He's hit all his teammates quickly and said, 'You guys got it,' and we'll roll from there."

Wolves coach Chris Finch said before Wednesday's loss to Golden State that the Edwards news was "a bit of a shock to everybody." Finch, however, feels confident that his team has the depth and experience to navigate an extended stretch without Edwards.

"We'll have to kind of fill that scoring void by committee," Finch said. "Certainly, spreading more shots around the team, everybody likes that. Obviously they've got to go in to make up the point difference."

Information from the Associated Press was used in this report.

articles.headline: PSG's Luis Enrique: Vitinha deserved higher Ballon d'Or ranking
articles.description: Paris Saint-Germain boss Luis Enrique does not believe star midfielder Vitinha got the recognition he deserved in the Ballon d'Or rankings.
articles.headlineJa: PSGのルイス・エンリケ監督、ヴィティーニャはバロンドールでより高い順位にふさわしかったと主張
articles.descriptionJa: パリ・サンジェルマンのルイス・エンリケ監督は、スターミッドフィルダーのヴィティーニャがバロンドールのランキングで正当な評価を得られたと考えていない。
articles.body:
Paris Saint-Germain boss Luis Enrique does not believe star midfielder Vitinha got the recognition he deserved in the Ballon d'Or rankings.

The back-to-back Champions League winners head to rock-bottom Le Havre on Friday evening having moved top of Ligue 1 with last weekend's 2-0 win against Lyon.

PSG return to action fresh from being crowned Men's Club of the Year at the 70th Ballon d'Or ceremony, when 10 of their players were among the 30 nominees for the men's award.

Vitinha was among those and ended up 14th, a year on from finishing third when team-mate Ousmane Dembélé lifted the trophy.

PSG boss Enrique said of the Portugal international: "It's a real pleasure to have a player with such technical and physical ability. His level is incredible.

"We're very pleased to have a player of his calibre, even though he wasn't ranked as highly as he deserves to be in the Ballon d'Or rankings."

Sixth-placed Khvicha Kvaratskhelia was PSG's highest-ranked player at the Ballon d'Or and this week underwent surgery in Qatar on a torn anterior cruciate ligament.

Dembélé finished seventh and is another missing for Friday's game at Le Havre, as are Nuno Mendes and Marquinhos after recording 23rd and 25th place finishes.

PSG said the trio "all continue their rehabilitation" and head coach Enrique said: "We like to have as much control as possible, and the issue of injuries has been a major focus of our work in recent years.

"Some players suffer injuries more frequently than others, so it can sometimes be difficult to control. We aim to refine and optimise the training load to minimise the number of injured players.

"Throughout my coaching career, we've always sought to manage this; there have been tough times and better times, but I'm pleased with what we're trying to achieve.

"However, it's always difficult because injuries are part and parcel of top-flight football."

PSG have the strength in depth to cope, even with a Champions League match at Villarreal and home game against Troyes following the perennial Ligue 1 champions' game at winless Le Havre.

Enrique knows the pressure is on them to stay in their "favourite position" and wants to continue building as they head to the Stade Océane seeking a ninth straight win in all competitions.

articles.headline: Raiders and Jets will try to stop struggles and quiet some outside noise when they square off Sunday
articles.description: — Las Vegas Raiders fans are getting restless, while New York Jets fans are fully frustrated.
articles.headlineJa: 日曜日に激突するレイダースとジェッツ、苦戦からの脱却と周囲の雑音を払拭することを目指す
articles.descriptionJa: ラスベガス・レイダースのファンに焦燥感が広がる一方、ニューヨーク・ジェッツのファンは完全な不満状態にある。
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- — Las Vegas Raiders fans are getting restless, while New York Jets fans are fully frustrated.


              Something's got to give. Right?


              The struggling squads square off Sunday at MetLife Stadium with each looking to get their season on track — as outside noise starts to grow louder.


              The Raiders (3-4) have dropped four straight after a surprising 3-0 start and some fans are calling for rookie Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick in April, to take over at quarterback to provide a spark. Kirk Cousins hasn't been bad, by any means — he leads the NFL with 16 touchdown passes — and coach Klint Kubiak shut down any chatter this week by saying the 38-year-old veteran would remain under center and “there is no controversy.”


              “I’ve seen the production," Kubiak said. "The production’s there. But it’s a team game, so we’ve got to produce together in order to win football games.”


              Same for the Jets (2-5), who have dropped two in a row, including a 28-25 defeat at home last Sunday to previously winless Miami. That loss fired up an already simmering seat under Aaron Glenn, who's 5-19 as New York's coach and might need an impressive run over the final two months to save his job.


              “I’ve been around a lot of good coaches and a lot of good leaders and I’ve said it a lot, I think A.G. is one of the best I’ve ever been around," center Josh Myers said. "I still believe that and I’ll continue believing that.”


              Geno Smith will see some familiar faces across the field after being the Raiders' starting quarterback last season, when he led the NFL with 17 interceptions. He was acquired by the Jets in the offseason and has respectable numbers — 10 touchdown passes, two INTs, 1,623 yards passing and a 70% completion rate — but the offense is struggling with consistency.


              Perhaps this week New York, ranked 23rd in yards per game, can get things going while facing a Las Vegas defense that's tied for 29th in yards allowed.


              “They’re a really good team and we’re not taking them lightly,” said Raiders defensive end Maxx Crosby, who added that he likes where the Raiders are at mentally. “Adversity reveals who you are. ... You can’t fall into the negativity. You've got to be positive, regardless of what the world wants you to feel like. 


              "So the only way to change that is go win and go be at your best, so that’s what we plan on doing.”


              Need to know
              Las Vegas (3-4) at New York Jets (2-5)


              When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EST, Fox.


              Latest odds: Jets by 1 1/2.


              Against the spread: Raiders 5-2; Jets 4-2-1.


              Last week: Raiders lost to Rams 35-21; Jets lost to Dolphins 28-25.


              Last meeting: Jets won 16-12 on Nov. 12, 2023, in Las Vegas.


              Series record: Raiders lead 27-20-2.

articles.headline: In Pittsburgh, the Browns chase a rare win and sole possession of the AFC North lead
articles.description: — Time to find out if the Cleveland Browns are for real.
articles.headlineJa: ピッツバーグでの一戦で、ブラウンズは久々の勝利とAFC北地区単独首位を狙う
articles.descriptionJa: クリーブランド・ブラウンズが本物かどうかを見極める時が来た。
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH -- — Time to find out if the Cleveland Browns are for real. 


              Maybe the Pittsburgh Steelers too.


              A month after the Browns pulled off a last-second home victory over their longtime rivals, an upset in name only at a place the Steelers have struggled to win of late, Cleveland (5-2) heads two hours south to Pittsburgh (5-2) with first place in the AFC North on the line.


              It's still far too early to start talking about the playoffs, sure. Yet Cleveland is well aware of what's at stake in a stadium where they've won just twice since it opened in 2001.


              “Another opportunity for us to go out there and play and try to get a win for the city and showcase that we’re a team that we can play in this league at a top level,” quarterback Deshaun Watson said.


              A level this iteration of the Browns has never seen, at least at the season's midpoint. Cleveland hasn't been 6-2 after eight games since 1994, back when Bill Belichick was a young head coach still finding his way and about a year before the franchise packed up and moved to Baltimore.


              The Browns have turned things around behind a gritty defense and a steady dose of some late-game heroics by Watson. All five of Cleveland's wins have been decided in the fourth quarter, including a 27-24 thriller on the road last week in Tennessee.


              The Titans, however, are struggling. The Steelers are not. While they've not been particularly dominant so far in head coach Mike McCarthy's first year, they've responded to the loss in Cleveland by ripping off three straight workmanlike victories while remaining very much a work in progress.


              Quarterback Aaron Rodgers has stressed repeatedly that there is room for improvement on offense, which has bogged down in the red zone and whose lone touchdown run of the season came on a 50-yard sprint by Jaylen Warren against Indianapolis three weeks ago.


              Still, when it has mattered late, the Steelers have found a way. They scored the last 10 points to pull away from the Colts, rallied from 13 down in the fourth quarter to edge Tampa Bay and expertly drained the final 5:52 off the clock in Paris last Sunday to turn away the Saints.


              “When you’re growing up, for me my favorite players all had the ball in their hands late in the game,” Rodgers said. “Quarterback, guard, Michael Jordan, pitchers, because you know that’s the guy making the impact. And so, in the fourth quarter, you want the ball in your hands and have a chance to win the game.”


              The winner on Sunday will be alone at the top of one of the most competitive divisions in the NFL as November opens. If the Browns can sweep the Steelers, it will validate their status as legitimate contenders. articles.headline: Dolphins look to build momentum against defending AFC champion Patriots as Willis faces former coach
articles.description: — Most of the current players on the Miami Dolphins roster haven't faced the New England Patriots very much.
articles.headlineJa: ドルフィンズ、AFC王者パトリオッツ戦で勢いづきを狙う。ウィリスは元コーチと対峙
articles.descriptionJa: 現在のマイアミ・ドルフィンズのロースターに名を連ねる選手の多くは、ニューイングランド・パトリオッツとの対戦経験が少ない。
articles.body:
MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. -- — Most of the current players on the Miami Dolphins roster haven't faced the New England Patriots very much. 


              But coach Jeff Hafley wants his young team to understand the significance of divisional matchups — especially Sunday's game against a Patriots team that has accomplished nearly everything Hafley hopes the Dolphins will some day. 


              “I’d be lying to you if I (said I) didn’t feel like I had to teach them about division play and the division,” Hafley said. “All these guys watched them play in the Super Bowl last year. I mean, we have 15 rookies. I hope they all watch the Super Bowl — who knows nowadays — but I’d imagine they all understand that team just went to the Super Bowl and they’re the reigning champs in our conference.”


              Vrabel had praise for Hafley and the Dolphins, who are coming off their first win of the season after beating the New York Jets. It was the best game of the season for quarterback Malik Willis, who threw for 208 yards, two touchdowns and rushed for a score.


              “They play extremely hard. I have a lot of respect for what Jeff’s done,” Vrabel said, “and probably a unique set of circumstances, which they’ve kind of admitted to. ... I think that they’ve continued to improve, and I know that they’re probably — and they should be – excited to play at home in front of their crowd. We’ll have to go on the road inside the division here and continue to improve.”


              Vrabel coached Willis in Tennessee during the Miami quarterback's first two seasons in the NFL. 


              The Titans traded up in 2022 to draft Willis out of Liberty in the third round while Ryan Tannehill was still the starter. Willis made three starts as a rookie, never throwing for more than 99 yards. The following season, Tennessee drafted Will Levis, and Willis was eventually traded to Green Bay.


              “I can’t say anything but great things about Coach Vrabel,” Willis said. “He taught me a lot about ball in general in this league, at this level. So I can’t be any type of way toward him. Obviously, he had to do what the best thing was for his team at that point, in his opinion. You can’t control other people’s opinion. All you can do is keep working and when your opportunity arises, take advantage of it.”


              The Patriots haven’t been quite as dominant this season as they were last season, when they went 14-3 en route to a Super Bowl appearance. 


              They’re coming off a loss at Chicago that snapped a three-game win streak, and Vrabel said this week there may be some things the team isn’t able to improve on this season.


              “When I look at it from my perspective, it’s like, this is what we’ve seen from seven weeks,” Vrabel said Wednesday, “and we can yell and scream about it till we’re blue in the face, or we can coach it, and it’s maybe not going to change.”

articles.headline: Burrow, Bengals go into November with momentum as they host struggling Titans
articles.description: Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals find themselves in an unusual position going into November — healthy and with momentum.
articles.headlineJa: バロウ率いるベンガルズ、苦戦するタイタンズを本拠地で迎え、勢いに乗った状態で11月へ
articles.descriptionJa: ジョー・バロウ率いるシンシナティ・ベンガルズは、怪我人がおらず勢いもあるという、11月を迎えるにあたって異例とも言える好条件に恵まれている。
articles.body:
Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals find themselves in an unusual position going into November — healthy and with momentum.


              The Bengals are 4-2 going into Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans. That's a 180-degree shift from the past two seasons when they were 2-4.


              Burrow, who was also recovering from turf toe surgery at this time last year, has led the way. He leads the league with a 71.4% completion rate, is second with a 110.4 passer rating and tied for second with 15 touchdown passes entering Week 8.


              “I feel really good about our team and the guys we have in there,” Burrow said. “It’s all just about building on what you’ve done and getting better. You can’t make the same mistake twice and expect to build momentum.”


              The Bengals learned from their first-half mistakes in Baltimore, where they trailed 13-0 at halftime, and scored on their first five possessions of the second half to beat the Ravens 35-13.


              Burrow has two straight games where he has four touchdown passes and no interceptions. Tee Higgins and Dallas’ CeeDee Lamb are the only players to have multiple games with at least 145 receiving yards this season while Ja'Marr Chase and tight end Mike Gesicki are tied for the AFC lead in receiving touchdowns with five.


              The defense has also been stout by getting consistent pressure on quarterbacks despite having one of the lowest blitz rates in the league. The Bengals are one of five teams tied for the league lead with 21 sacks entering Week 8.


              Zac Taylor's squad is over .500 through six games for only the second time in his eight-year heading coaching tenure. The other was 2021, when they advanced to Super Bowl 56.


              Four of Cincinnati's five November opponents are under .500. Tennessee comes in 1-6 after last week's 27-24 loss to Cleveland after it had a 14-0 lead in the first quarter.


              Even though the Titans have gotten off to a slow start in Robert Saleh's first season as coach, all but two games have been decided by one score.


              “We just got to keep going through the process of learning how to finish. We have to learn,” Saleh said. “This organization hasn’t won two (straight) games since 2022, there’s been a lot of blowouts. So, we haven’t even been able to recognize or be put in those positions as often. We’ve had five ops (opportunities), we’re 1-4 in those opportunities. And hopefully as we continue to get these ops, they’ll recognize where we need to get better, not only from a preparation standpoint, but from a finishing standpoint.”


              One player the Bengals won't have to worry about is Jeffery Simmons, after he was traded by Tennessee to Chicago on Thursday. Simmons 21 quarterback pressures were the most among NFL defensive tackles entering Week 8.

articles.headline: Bears get Jeffery Simmons: Key intel on blockbuster trade
articles.description: Is Jeffery Simmons the key missing piece for the Bears' Super Bowl puzzle? Here are key takeaways from the blockbuster trade.
articles.headlineJa: ベアーズがジェフリー・シモンズを獲得：大型トレードに関する重要情報
articles.descriptionJa: ジェフリー・シモンズは、ベアーズがスーパーボウルを制するために欠けていた最後のピースとなるのか？この大型トレードの要点を解説する。
articles.body:
In a high-stakes game of poker before the NFL trade deadline on Nov. 10, Chicago Bears general manager Ryan Poles went all-in on Thursday after seeing two other NFC teams with legitimate Super Bowl aspirations make their moves.

Poles sent first-round picks in 2027 and '28 and a fourth-rounder in '27 to the Tennessee Titans for first-team All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons and a 2028 fifth-rounder. It's the first time in the common draft era (since 1967) a DT has been traded for multiple first-round picks, per ESPN Research.

The Bears now have the second-best chance to win the NFC at 13%, per ESPN Analytics. The San Francisco 49ers hold the best chance at 39% after trading for DT DeForest Buckner, and the Seattle Seahawks have the third-best number at 11% after trading for guard Quenton Nelson; both of those trades happened Tuesday. All three players are former first-round All-Pros.

Since coming into the NFL in 2019, Simmons' 46.5 sacks are the second most among defensive tackles behind Buckner. He should be a huge help for a Bears team that ranks 23rd in pass rush win rate from interior defenders this season (13% per ESPN Analytics/NFL Next Gen Stats).

For the Titans, it's a huge haul of draft capital as they plan for the years ahead. But will that future include the 2025 first overall pick, QB Cam Ward?

Bears reporter Courtney Cronin, Titans reporter Turron Davenport, and national analysts Ben Solak, Jeremy Fowler and Jordan Reid break down the trade from all angles.

Does this signal that the Bears believe it's Super Bowl or bust this season?

Chicago is 5-2 and entering a pivotal road matchup against the defending-champion Seahawks. The team now has the game-wrecking type of defender it had been lacking.

Poles has been aggressive throughout his tenure at the trade deadline, shipping off Roquan Smith and Robert Quinn to complete the full teardown of the roster in 2022 before aggressively adding at future deadlines, like when he acquired Montez Sweat for a second-round pick in 2023.

But this move is unlike any we've seen the Bears pull off over the past five seasons. Adding Simmons indicates the Bears are aiming to elevate themselves from a top-five team in the NFC into a franchise that can win a Lombardi Trophy with quarterback Caleb Williams still on his rookie contract. The Bears' offensive core is getting expensive. The team made Darnell Wright the highest-paid right tackle in NFL history (four years, $116 million) in August and will soon have to pay Williams, who is eligible for an extension following the 2026 season.

Chicago has one of the NFL's best offenses (first in rushing, third in yards, eighth in scoring) and believes it can take a defense that, despite ranking ninth in scoring and eighth in yards allowed, has struggled to pressure opposing quarterbacks. This turns a weak link into one of the best units in the league.

ESPN's basketball daily cheat sheet is your pregame destination before you lock in daily fantasy and betting decisions for that night's games. Here you'll find our top insights for the slate, including players to target for your daily fantasy rosters, along with game-by-game injury reports.

What you need to know for Thursday

Thursday's NBA schedule has just three games, but there are some interesting matchups. Two undefeated teams meet in Portland, two winless teams face off in New Orleans, and the Cleveland Cavaliers and Atlanta Hawks are both playing on the second night of a back-to-back.

The Cavaliers (3-1) have won three straight heading into their matchup against the Hawks (2-3). Evan Mobley finished with 24 points and 12 rebounds in Wednesday's win over Washington, while Peyton Watson added 22 points. The Hawks, meanwhile, have lost three consecutive games despite strong early-season production from Jalen Johnson.

The Sacramento Kings (0-4) and New Orleans Pelicans (0-4) are both looking for their first win. Zach LaVine has averaged 27.3 points per game for Sacramento. Zion Williamson and the Pelicans will be playing their second game in as many nights.

The Memphis Grizzlies (4-0) and Portland Trail Blazers (3-0) close out the night. Ty Jerome has been outstanding for the Grizzlies, averaging 29.8 points and 6.5 assists per game. But the biggest story is Ja Morant facing Memphis for the first time since being traded to Portland over the summer.

Let's take a closer look at Thursday's matchups, along with some fantasy streamers and betting angles worth considering.

Watson has scored at least 24 fantasy points in three consecutive games, including a season-high 45 fantasy points against the Minnesota Timberwolves on Monday. He's giving Cleveland more versatility on both ends of the floor, attacking the basket and creating opportunities for teammates while providing weak-side rim protection. That ability to contribute offensively and defensively should help him maintain a significant role in the rotation. Watson's steals and blocks make him particularly appealing in category leagues. Watson is worth streaming now but also deserves consideration as a longer-term hold.

articles.headline: Crystal Palace's Ismaïla Sarr set to be sidelined for weeks, Pierre Sage confirms
articles.description: Ismaïla Sarr is likely to remain sidelined with a groin issue until after the international break, Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage has confirmed.
articles.headlineJa: クリスタル・パレスのイスマイラ・サール、数週間の離脱へ。ピエール・サージュが認める
articles.descriptionJa: クリスタル・パレスのピエール・サージュ監督は、イスマイラ・サールが鼠径部の問題により、代表ウィーク明けまで戦線を離脱する可能性が高いことを認めた。
articles.body:
Ismaïla Sarr is likely to remain sidelined with a groin issue until after the international break, Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage has confirmed.

The Senegal international was last season's Conference League top scorer, but has made just five appearances for Palace across all competitions so far.

Palace have lost one of those five games, while they have been beaten in five of the eight matches he has missed, but the under-pressure Sage will have to do without him for at least the next three outings before the November international window.

When asked about when the 28-year-old might be available again, Sage said: "I think after the international break."

The under-pressure Eagles boss secured a big Carabao Cup win at Fulham on Wednesday night, and will now look to turn Palace's Premier League fortunes around at Tottenham before hosting Hoffenheim in the Europa League, then welcoming Liverpool to Selhurst Park before the pause.

Asked if he might prefer to be taking on their subsequent league opponents -- Coventry and Hull -- Sage said: "Every point smells good, and if we take points against Liverpool or Tottenham or against the other team, it's the same for us at the end, because we need, and we will play all the game to take points.

"We are not in a position to choose one game better than another. We do, we did, and we will do the same with the cups and the league too. That's why we made some rotations, because we wanted to win on Wednesday, but we wanted to create the conditions of freshness for Saturday too.

"At the moment that strategy is good, but we have to confirm that and go until the goal we fixed at the beginning of the week."

Sage confirmed Jean-Philippe Mateta was rested against Fulham but will be ready to start against Tottenham.

Jorgen Strand Larsen continues to recover from the ankle issue he sustained in their 2-2 draw with Besiktas last week, and will train with the group on Thursday afternoon.

Sage confirmed Quinten Timber could also potentially feature in the Spurs clash, which should also feature captain Dean Henderson who recovered well on his first start back from injury on Wednesday.

Palace sit one place and point clear of the relegation zone heading into Sunday's trip to north London, and there has been some suggestion that this weekend could be a major test of the front office's faith that Sage remains the right man for the job.

articles.headline: Man City, Bayern among the good, bad and lucky in Europe's top leagues
articles.description: We're a quarter of the way through the 2026-27 European season -- long enough to separate fact from fiction when it comes to from. Who's been lucky? Who's been good? Who's been both, or neither?
articles.body:
About a quarter of the way through the club season, your place in the table only means so much. In the Premier League and Bundesliga, 14 teams -- including Ipswich Town, Paderborn and even Tottenham Hotspur -- are within six points of the top four. In Ligue 1, it's 13. In LaLiga, 14 teams are within six points of the relegation zone. You can find some separation here and there, but we're just getting started, and we only have a partial picture of how things will end up.

We also know that the table is lying a little bit. We see funky results all the time, and they have an outsized impact when we're seen only a small portion of matches. Still, by this point in the 2026-27 campaign, each Big Five team has played hundreds and hundreds of possessions, and we know who is creating (or allowing) the best chances. Thanks to xG, we also know what that means.

Essentially, xG is a chance creation metric. It obviously doesn't guarantee success, especially in the short term, but over the long haul a team's ability to create superior shot quality and/or volume is more predictive than simply who's putting the ball in the net in a small sample. And by comparing who's generated the most points to who's created chance creation advantages, with a fun trend line in between, we can get a grasp of who is ahead of or behind where they should be.

Who's both lucky and good? Who's good, but unlucky? Who's the opposite?

Here are some xG standouts, for better or worse, in Europe's Big Five leagues.

- Jones: Vozinha's Ballon d'Or appearance was made for us

- Ogden: Man United are a mess. Where are the Glazers?

- Olley: Ballon d'Or is Kane's crowning moment

Lucky and good

Definition: Teams with an xG differential of at least +0.3 per game, but more points than expected

Lazio. Lazio have finished seventh or worse in Serie A for three straight years, and due to an ongoing fan protest of club president Claudio Lotito, they're averaging a league-worst home attendance of 9,515. They've also only dropped two points in nine league matches, and they're tied with Inter atop the table. Pretty wild stuff.

It's also probably unsustainable stuff.

While they've enjoyed a few genuinely dominant performances (like a 6-2 win at Sassuolo), they've also scored 22 goals from shots worth just 15.5 xG. Forward Tijjani Noslin, winger Gustav Isaksen and midfielder Kenneth Taylor have combined for nine goals from 3.9 xG; I probably don't have to spell out how unsustainable that is. Lazio have stockpiled enough points to remain in the Champions League hunt for a while, but there's a goal-scoring slump in their future, whether or not there are fans in the stands to see it.

Atletico Madrid. Diego Simeone scoffs at your advanced stats. Over the past 12 full seasons, Atletico have produced a goal differential higher -- and in some cases, much higher -- than their xG differential 11 times. In fact, over the Simeone era, their GD in league play (+504) is 46% higher than their xGD (+346.0). Dark

articles.headline: Former Man United midfielder Herrera on City breaches: 'Damage irreparable'
articles.description: Former Manchester United midfielder Ander Herrera is bitter over the EPL title he was deprived of during Manchester City's decade of rules breaching.
articles.headlineJa: 元マン・ユナイテッドのMFヘレラ、シティの違反について「取り返しのつかない損害」と語る
articles.descriptionJa: 元マンチェスター・ユナイテッドのミッドフィールダー、アンデル・ヘレラは、マンチェスター・シティによる長年の規約違反の間に奪われたプレミアリーグのタイトルに対し、憤りを感じている。
articles.body:
Former Manchester United midfielder Ander Herrera is bitter over the Premier League title that he was deprived of during Manchester City's decade of rules breaching.

Manchester City were last month found guilty on almost all of the 100-plus charges of serious breaches of Premier League financial regulations between 2009 and 2018.

Herrera, who played for Manchester United from 2014 until 2019 and is now on the books of Real Zaragoza, told the Mario Suárez podcast: "I would have a Premier League title.

"It really changes the picture when you have a Premier League [title]."

There have been calls for Manchester City to be stripped of the three Premier League titles won during the nine-year period. Herrera won four trophies in his five years at Old Trafford but the Premier League was not one of them.

Under José Mourinho, Manchester United finished second, 19 points adrift of City in the 2017-18 campaign.

"It was the year [2018] when Mourinho said that bit about 'I give a lot of credit to this second-place finish because nobody knows what's going on behind the scenes'," Herrera, 37, said.

"Mou [Mourinho]'s like The Simpsons -- whatever he says, it ends up happening. And he'd already been saying that something strange was going on.

"You have to follow the rules, and what was happening wasn't right -- we all realised that. I've had friends who've come to Manchester and they couldn't get tickets to go to Old Trafford, yet the ones for the Etihad were being given away for free. They don't have the fan base, but they spend as if they did..."

Herrera said he sympathises with Manchester City players and staff.

"Nothing to say about the players, nothing to say about the manager [Pep Guardiola]," the Spaniard said. "They deserve all the credit in the world for what they've achieved.

"If I were a Manchester City player, I'd be angry; I'd be furious with those in charge because they've tarnished and cast doubt on everything the team has achieved over the years."

Sanctions have not yet been announced but Herrera agrees with former Manchester United teammate Wayne Rooney that the punishment must be significant considering the "irreparable damage" it caused other clubs.

"For me, it has to be something big, something that sets a precedent -- as Rooney said recently," Herrera said.

"It has to set a precedent so that the next person who says, 'I'm going to inflate the revenue illegally' will think, 'No, I won't do it because I'll get relegated.'

"Nottingham Forest were sanctioned [with a four-point deduction in the 2022-23]; Everton were sanctioned [with a 10-point deduction in the 2021-22 season].

"The damage they [Man City] have caused is obviously irreparable.

"In terms of revenue, Tottenham finished fifth for three consecutive years and failed to qualify for the Champions League. That has a significant financial impact on Tottenham."

articles.headline: Debunk or double down? Judging 10 early-season NBA overreactions
articles.description: A 29-year-old is the NBA's next breakout star. Miami's Giannis era is already cooked. And so are the Thunder, Knicks and Warriors. Which overreactions are valid?
articles.headlineJa: 間違いか、それとも確信か？シーズン序盤のNBAにおける10の過剰反応を検証
articles.descriptionJa: 29歳の選手がNBAの次なるブレイクスターになる。マイアミのヤニス時代はすでに終わっている。サンダー、ニックス、ウォリアーズも同様だ。どの過剰反応が妥当だろうか？
articles.body:
Welcome to the final days of October, featuring falling leaves, early sunsets, Halloween decorations illuminating the night -- and the yearly pastime of overreacting to the first week of a new NBA season.

After all, small sample size theatre has provided early gems such as:

The sky is falling in Oklahoma City, New York and Miami!

The three-guard experiment in San Antonio needs to go!

Charlotte is already better without LaMelo Ball!

Ty Jerome? Ty Jerome!

With those early storylines and more in mind, let's examine 10 popular overreactions to the young 2026-27 season -- and determine which have staying power. (Note: stats through Tuesday's games.)

The Miami Heat will finish with their worst record since 2008.

Zach Kram: Not an overreaction

For reference, 2007-08 was the last time the Heat finished with fewer than 37 wins, the season that they tanked down the stretch to go 15-67 in a futile attempt to land Derrick Rose in the draft.

Merely by the law of averages, the 2026-27 Heat are bound to improve. They've had the seventh-worst shooting luck on offense, according to GeniusIQ tracking, and the second-worst shooting luck on defense. Miami is actually forcing teams into tough shots, but its opponents have been on fire regardless, making 53% of their midrange shots and 40% of their 3s, per Cleaning the Glass.

On the other hand, the Heat's offense has been stuck in the mud even accounting for that poor shooting luck, and guard Davion Mitchell is the only role player who looks comfortable playing with Giannis Antetokounmpo. There's time for that to change -- but as of Wednesday, ESPN's Basketball Power Index predicts the Heat will finish the season with just 38 wins. That's already down from 46 projected wins in the preseason, and just one ahead of this historical franchise benchmark.

Ben Golliver: Overreaction

Let's be clear: The Antetokounmpo era in South Beach is off to an atrocious start. Instead of building off its blockbuster trade for the two-time MVP with a transformative offseason, the Heat lost Norman Powell to the Chicago Bulls in free agency and settled for adding Klay Thompson, who is a shell of his former self at age 36. On the court, it's already clear that the Heat need another proven ball handler and more shooting, and Antetokounmpo needs more time to jell with Bam Adebayo.

Despite all those challenges, it's reasonable to give Heat coach Erik Spoelstra and his staff a long runway. Antetokounmpo's need to dominate the ball has clashed with the free-flowing offensive system that Miami utilized in 2025-26, and several veteran players seem to be easing into the new season. Spoelstra is a tinkerer who has conjured winning records from less talented rosters, and he'll be willing to trust his younger options if Miami's offensive struggles persist.

articles.headline: Fantasy basketball: Seven preseason assumptions already being challenged
articles.description: The fantasy basketball experts go over what hasn't gone as planned during the opening week of the NBA season.
articles.body:
Sometimes, it takes a while to see how the things are going to shake out in this new NBA season. Other times, it is plainly obvious that things are not as they seemed before the season officially tipped off, whether that means less playing time, a drop in production, or changes under a new coaching staff.

With that in mind, we asked our fantasy basketball experts Andre Snellings, Eric Moody, Eric Karabell, Steve Alexander, Jim McCormick and Michael F. Florio to identify the biggest preseason assumptions that are already being challenged.

Here's what has stood out to them after one week of NBA action.

Tyrese Maxey, other 76ers thriving despite Philadelphia's star power

Moody: The concern in Philadelphia was that too many stars would eat into Maxey's production. LeBron James and Jaylen Brown joined Joel Embiid, but Maxey averaged 50 fantasy points per game through four games as the Sixers opened 3-1. Brown contributed 36.0 fantasy points per game, and Embiid recorded a 28-point triple-double against the Milwaukee Bucks last Saturday. There will be nights when someone sacrifices touches, but Maxey hasn't looked like the player making that sacrifice.

Florio: While LeBron and Embiid have already missed a game and that was a big fear, they have performed extremely well so far, especially in Roto formats. Maxey is a Top 5 player in all formats, while Embiid and Brown are each averaging over 20 PPG. LeBron James continues to contribute across the board. It's still early, but fading them in fantasy is one early season regret.

Giannis' arrival is already affecting Adebayo's production

Karabell: Perhaps I hadn't considered the potential statistical downside of what superstar Giannis Antetokoumpo joining the Miami Heat would mean for longtime underrated star Bam Adebayo. So far, the fit looks awkward. Adebayo averaged 20.1 PPG and 10 RPG last season, continuing a seven-season run of excellence. Is that over now? Bam is off to a terrible start (11.8 PPG, 7.3 RPG, 40% FG, 61.5% FT), and oh, Miami is winless. These numbers must improve, but how much? Is Bam still a top 50 fantasy option? Maybe so, maybe not.

Alex Sarr will have to wait to reach new heights

Snellings: Sarr is unlikely to approach, let alone build on, his breakout campaign from last season if the Washington Wizards are fully healthy. After averaging 16.3 PPG, 7.4 RPG and 2.0 BPG last season, he is currently averaging 8.8 PPG, 5.3 RPG and 1.3 BPG in this one. With Anthony Davis occupying all the spaces Sarr prefers but at much higher volume, Sarr just doesn't have the shots (6.5 FGA this season, down from 13.7 FGA last year), rebounding or shot-blocking opportunities to approach what he did last season. And number one overall pick AJ Dybantsa hasn't even played yet this season, so once he's in the fold Sarr may get even fewer looks.
